app/src/env.d.ts.content: The PackFrontendContribution interface is duplicated across two module declarations with inconsistent shapes (one has `name`, the other does not). Consider defining it once and reusing to avoid drift.

The `vanblog` property on `Window` is typed as always present, unlike the old `__pb` which was `VanblogClient | undefined`. If the initialization script fails to load, accessing `window.vanblog.pb` will throw at runtime with no TypeScript warning. Consider keeping it optional: `vanblog?: { pb: ... }`.

app/src/lib/frontCardSurface.ts.content: This file contains only explanatory comments with no functional code, and is not imported or referenced anywhere in the codebase. It serves as dead code that clutters the project. Consider deleting this file entirely rather than keeping it as a comment-only placeholder. Git history already preserves the deleted implementation.

app/src/loaders/posts.ts.content: Using `result.items.indexOf(post)` inside `.map()` callback has O(n²) complexity. The `.map()` callback already provides the index as its second argument — use that instead for both better performance and clarity.

When `post.id` is falsy in `loadCollection`, the per-post cache tag (`post:${post.id}`) is omitted, but a synthetic `id` is still generated on line 84. If an update occurs, Astro won't know to invalidate this entry because no specific tag was emitted. Use the same synthetic id for the cache tag so invalidation can work correctly.

app/src/lib/routing-editor.js.content:
The change from `window.__pb` to `self.vanblog.pb` introduces a potential TypeError. Previously, if the global was unset, `pb` would simply be `undefined` and the null check at line 223 (`if (!pb) return alert("未登录")`) would handle it gracefully. Now, if `self.vanblog` hasn't been initialized (e.g., `initClient()` fails or the script loads before AdminLayout), `self.vanblog.pb` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'pb')`, crashing the entire editor before any guard can run.

Consider adding a defensive check: `const pb = self.vanblog?.pb;`

Loose equality `==` is used here to check for both `null` and `undefined`. While this is a well-known JavaScript idiom, the project's code standards require strict equality (`===`). Use an explicit check instead.

app/src/dispatcher/index.mjs.content:
The in-flight request tracking in `server.on('request', ...)` adds `done` to `inFlightRequests` for every request, including fast-path responses (health check, static file 304/404) that complete synchronously inside the `createServer` callback. Since the second listener fires *after* the `createServer` callback returns, responses that already called `res.end()` will never emit the `'finish'`/`'close'`/`'error'` events, so `done` is never removed from the set. This causes:
1. A slow memory leak (one leaked function reference per fast request).
2. Graceful shutdown always hits the 10-second timeout because `inFlightRequests.size` never reaches 0.

Suggestion: Check `res.writableEnded` before adding `done` to skip already-completed responses.

`createReadStream(filePath).pipe(res)` does not attach an error handler to the read stream. If the file becomes inaccessible between the `statSync` check and the actual read (e.g., deletion, permission change, disk error), the stream emits an `'error'` event. Without a handler, this becomes an uncaught exception (logged but not responded to) or, in newer Node.js versions, can crash the process. The client receives no proper HTTP error status.

Suggestion: Attach an error handler that sets an appropriate status code and ends the response.

`server.listen()` does not have an `'error'` event listener. If the port is already in use (EADDRINUSE) or the process lacks permissions (EACCES), Node.js emits an `'error'` event on the server. Without a listener, this becomes an uncaught exception caught by the global handler which deliberately does NOT exit. The process remains alive but is unable to serve traffic. The entrypoint's health check (`wait_for`) eventually detects the failure after 30 seconds and kills the container, but an immediate exit would be cleaner and faster.

Suggestion: Add an `'error'` listener that logs the error and calls `process.exit(1)`.

The MIME type lookup table is missing an entry for `.mjs` (ECMAScript module) files. If a theme build produces client-side `.mjs` files, they will be served as `application/octet-stream` instead of `text/javascript` (or `application/javascript`). Browsers may refuse to execute them, breaking theme functionality.

Suggestion: Add `'.mjs': 'text/javascript'` (or `'application/javascript'`) to the `MIME_TYPES` map.

In the main request handler's catch block, when `res.headersSent` is true, the response is silently left dangling — no `res.end()` or `res.destroy()` is called. The client will hang waiting for a response that will never complete.

Suggestion: Call `res.destroy()` or `res.end()` to terminate the hanging connection when headers have already been sent and an error occurs.

app/src/styles/global.css.content:
The `not-dark` variant definition `(&:where(:not(.dark), :not(.dark) *))` incorrectly matches elements inside a `.dark` container. Both branches — `:not(.dark)` (element itself lacks `.dark`) and `:not(.dark) *` (descendant of a non-`.dark` ancestor) — will match almost everything in a `<html class="dark">` document because `<body>` and children lack `.dark` themselves. This means `not-dark:` styles will leak into dark mode, producing the opposite of the intended behavior.

The correct negation of the `dark` variant's `(:where(.dark, .dark *))` is `(&:not(:where(.dark, .dark *)))`, which selects elements only when no ancestor has `.dark`.
